outline: What an API is and its importance
Application interaction with AI via APIs

slides.title: Welcome to Building: Understanding APIs
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Building: Understanding **APIs**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,

• Define what an **API** is and its fundamental purpose.

• Explain the roles of **prompts** and **API keys** in **API** interactions.

• Describe the typical flow of how applications use **APIs** to send requests and receive **AI**-generated responses.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have knowledge of Episode 1: Python basics for **API**.

slides.title: Understanding APIs: The Digital Connector
slides.narration:
What if different software needed to talk to each other?
How would they communicate?
An **API** acts as a digital connector.
Think of an **API** like a waiter in a restaurant.
You give your order to the waiter.
The waiter takes it to the kitchen, which is another system.
Then, the waiter brings your meal back to you.
Similarly, an **API** takes your request to another software.
It then brings the response back to your application.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing an API as a waiter connecting a customer (application) to a kitchen (another software system)

slides.title: Prompts and API Keys: Your Instructions and Access
slides.narration:
With that understanding, let's see how we talk to an **API**.
We use something called a **prompt**.
A **prompt** is simply an instruction or a question.
You send this **prompt** through the **API**.
But how does the **API** know who you are?
This is where **API keys** come in.
An **API key** is like a unique digital ID.
It gives you secure access to the **API** service.
Think of it as your secure pass.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a user giving an instruction (prompt) and presenting a key (API key) to unlock access to a service

slides.title: Application Flow: Sending Requests, Receiving AI Responses
slides.narration:
Now, let's put it all together.
How does your application use an **API**?
First, your application sends a request.
This request includes your **prompt** and your **API key**.
The **API** receives this request.
It then sends your **prompt** to an **AI** model.
The **AI** model processes your instruction.
It generates a response.
Finally, the **API** sends this **AI**-generated response back to your application.
This is how applications get intelligent answers.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a step-by-step flow: application sends request with prompt and API key, API forwards to AI model, AI processes and responds, API sends response back to application

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We understood that an **API** is a digital connector between software.
We also learned about **prompts** as instructions.
**API keys** provide secure access to services.
Finally, we saw how applications send requests.
They receive **AI**-generated responses through **APIs**.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Think of any application you use daily.
Consider how it might use an **API**.
What requests could it send?
What responses might it receive?
Compare the results.
